audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 matches 48.99% over 4464 games. The lane is one clean level and then a wall: Shield of Durand at level 2 is a taunt plus a magic shield against a kit that is entirely magic damage, and it only gets worse into MR items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Galio at Level 1 and 'Skill' on the other six rows. The content layer and the packet both read Katarina at Level 1 and Galio on all six after. Level 1 was inverted and the other six were blank — and all six whys described Katarina winning stages the packet gives to Galio.
audit.why: Level 1 is genuinely Katarina's: Shield of Durand does not exist yet and his Q is a waveclear tool at 60 mana. From level 2 the taunt exists and every melee commit her kit depends on is punishable, which is exactly where the packet flips.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Katarina, phases[1..6].side -> Galio, ratings moved with them, and all six flipped whys rewritten in the same proposal so no row argues with the sentence under it. win[0..6] already holds these values on disk.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page built the whole matchup around Justice Punch — focus, loading, cooldowns, report[5] — when the ability that actually decides it is Shield of Durand. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit, dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted under 'Keep W speed as the spacing tool', and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted under 'Shunpo in with both uses spent'.
audit.why: Katarina's R is flagged channel-interruptible and Galio's W is a taunt: that is a hard cancel of Death Lotus on an 18s cooldown at rank 1, against her 75s ultimate at rank 1. The same W also carries a magic shield, and every point of Katarina's damage is magic — so it blunts the burst and ends the channel with one button. Justice Punch is only his engage. Riot's text also makes Colossal Smash an empowered next attack, so his opening is a wind-up, not a cast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt around W 18s->14s, E 11s and R 180/160/140; the taunt-cancels-channel rule stated in tradeBad, dontsFull[0].d, enemyWin and report[5].t; the passive wind-up tell added to report[5].t.
